glossary.covered: chain-target permits all of this traffic.
glossary.partial: chain-target permits only part of this traffic (some addresses or ports are missing).
glossary.shadowed: An earlier chain-target rule blocks this traffic before a permit is reached.
glossary.denied: chain-target has a rule that blocks this traffic.
glossary.missing: chain-target has no rule for this traffic; its default action drops it.
glossary.wrong way: chain-target would send this subnet to the internet, not inside.
glossary.no route on B: chain-target has no route for this subnet.
glossary.other inside interface: chain-target routes this subnet inside, but out of a different inside interface.
glossary.over-permitted: chain-target allows more than Edge + DC firewall.
glossary.over-permitted (partial): chain-target allows part of this traffic that Edge + DC firewall does not.
glossary.also on A: Edge + DC firewall allows this traffic too.
glossary.inactive on B: chain-target has the NAT but it is disabled.
glossary.mapped conflict: The public IP is already used by a different inside host on chain-target.
glossary.mapped reuse: chain-target uses the same public IP as Edge + DC firewall (only valid when both share the public subnet).
glossary.mapped outside B public: chain-target's NAT uses a public IP outside chain-target's public ranges.
glossary.differs: chain-target has a NAT for this host, but with different addresses.
glossary.action unknown (L7): The rule has application/URL/user conditions; its real action (allow or block) is only in FMC.
glossary.blocked (L7): Marked as a block rule: left out of the compare and the plan.
glossary.same name, different value: The object exists on both, with different addresses.
